citations.quote: In the variance–covariance method the risk-factor changes Xt+1 are assumed to follow a multivariate normal distribution
The variance–covariance method offers a simple solution to the risk-measurement problem, but this convenience is achieved at the cost of two crude simplifying assumptions.

frontmatter_snapshot.summary: Parametric (variance–covariance / delta-normal) VaR assumes the risk-factor changes are multivariate normal so the linearised portfolio loss is itself normal and VaR reads off as a closed-form quantile; McNeil flags its two crude simplifications — linearisation error and an unrealistic normality assumption for heavy-tailed financial returns.
frontmatter_snapshot.title: Parametric (Variance-Covariance) VaR — McNeil Ch.9 §9.2.2
